subject: Learning Methods
title: Feynman's Learning Secret
description: A micro-lesson that makes Feynman's Learning Secret usable.

hook.text: Richard Feynman won the Nobel Prize and was called 'The Great Explainer.' His secret method was disarmingly simple.

buildup.text: Feynman said: if you cannot explain something simply, you don't understand it well enough. Simplicity reveals mastery.

discovery.text: His technique: write the concept in your own words as if teaching a child. Use no jargon. Only plain language.

twist.text: The hard part is honesty. Jargon often masks confusion. Removing it exposes exactly which pieces you truly understand.

climax.text: Pick any concept you are studying. Write a one-paragraph explanation for a ten year old. Where you struggle is gold.

quiz.question: What is the core principle of Feynman's learning technique?
options: Read the original research papers, not textbooks
Explain the concept in plain language as if teaching a child
Practice solving problems without looking at examples
